# Website project instructions

## Project purpose
This repository contains my personal academic and professional website, published through GitHub Pages.

My existing Google Sites website at https://www.anthonycruz.org/ is the primary design and content reference. My goals are:
1. To fully migrate away from Google Sites to this GitHub Pages-hosted website, maintaining the same content and transferring the URL.
2. To enable blogging using Jekyll.

## Visual identity
- Aim for a polished, contemporary, intellectually engaging academic website.
- Use a restrained palette of deep forest green, warm neutrals, white, and near-black.
- Prioritize readability, whitespace, clear hierarchy, and a consistent visual language.
- Convey expertise in cognitive psychology, learning, memory, research, and science communication.
- Keep the presentation accessible, human, and professional rather than overly corporate or neuroscience-themed.

## Implementation
- Inspect the existing repository before proposing changes.
- Preserve the current GitHub Pages publishing setup and existing working functionality.
- Reuse existing HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and assets wherever practical.
- Prefer simple, maintainable solutions over unnecessary frameworks or dependencies.
- Ensure responsive layouts for mobile, tablet, and desktop.
- Follow semantic HTML and accessibility best practices.
- Preserve existing page content, links, metadata, and navigation unless a change is explicitly requested.
- Do not invent biographical details, academic credentials, publications, awards, or research findings.
- Check internal links, image paths, typography, and layout consistency when making changes.

## Workflow
- Explain the proposed approach before making major structural changes.
- Make focused, reviewable changes rather than rewriting the entire site unnecessarily.
- Do not commit, push, or publish changes without my explicit approval.
- Summarize modified files and explain how to preview and test the result.
